argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0108c: meeting "c" (conceptual design) of series SY0108.

PROJECT
The team is designing a voice-controlled kitchen timer.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Project Manager (PM)  Helen  present
B  Industrial Designer (ID)  Marcus  present
C  Marketing Expert (ME)  Priya  present
D  User Interface designer (UI)  Tom  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0108a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, and the team members introduced themselves in their roles as project manager, industrial designer, marketing expert and user interface designer. The project manager introduced the project, a hands-free voice-controlled kitchen timer with a target selling price of around 20 euros and a production cost under 10 euros per unit, and explained the four-meeting structure. The team discussed initial requirements: an alarm loud enough to hear over an extractor fan, a microphone that can pick up the user over kitchen noise, and voice commands to set, cancel and query the timer. The industrial designer said voice recognition is feasible within budget if a cheap offline chip recognising a small fixed set of commands is used, and the team agreed the timer should be voice-first with a physical backup button. The team practised with the whiteboard drawing tool, assigned individual tasks, and scheduled the functional design meeting for Friday at 10:00, revised from an earlier plan of Thursday at 14:00 because the industrial designer has a supplier visit on Thursday afternoon.
  decisions: The next meeting (functional design) will be held on Friday at 10:00; this replaces the earlier agreed Thursday 14:00 slot. The timer will be primarily voice-controlled but will include at least one physical backup button. Voice recognition will be kept simple, using a low-cost offline chip that recognises a small fixed set of commands.
  actions: The industrial designer will research components (voice recognition chip, microphone, speaker, battery) and their approximate costs, including the cheapest adequate recognition module. The industrial designer will investigate battery versus mains power, given the drain of an always-listening microphone. The user interface designer will draft a voice command list and define what the timer displays or says back. The marketing expert will research user requirements for kitchen timers and review competing products on the market. The marketing expert will run a quick survey of around ten people who cook a lot, with early responses by the next meeting. The project manager will write up and circulate the minutes along with a new invitation for the Friday 10:00 meeting.
  problems: Whether the timer should support multiple simultaneous timers was parked for the functional design meeting, as it complicates the command set. Whether a wake word is needed was raised but not settled. Battery versus mains power is undecided and affects the display design. Meeting the under-10-euro production cost with voice recognition, a loud alarm and a noise-robust microphone remains to be confirmed.
  action item SY0108a.ai1: Research components (voice recognition chip, microphone, speaker, battery) and approximate costs, including the cheapest adequate recognition module. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0108a.ai2: Investigate battery versus mains power given the drain of an always-listening microphone. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0108a.ai3: Draft a voice command list and define what the timer displays or says back. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0108a.ai4: Research user requirements for kitchen timers and review competing products. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0108a.ai5: Run a quick survey of about ten people who cook a lot, with early responses by the Friday meeting. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0108a.ai6: Write up and circulate the minutes with a new invitation for the Friday 10:00 meeting. (owner A, active)
  fact (plan_change): The next meeting was first agreed for Thursday at 14:00, then moved to Friday at 10:00 because the industrial designer is visiting a supplier on Thursday afternoon.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed supporting multiple simultaneous timers; it was parked for the functional design meeting.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert raised using a wake word such as "hey timer"; the industrial designer said it is probably needed, but it was not decided.

[SY0108b, functional design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the functional design meeting and noted that the marketing expert was absent through illness, so no user requirements or survey results could be presented; the team agreed to continue on the technical side and flag anything needing marketing input. The industrial designer reported component costs from his supplier visit: an offline voice recognition chip at 2.50 euros handling about twenty phrases plus one wake word, a noise-cancelling microphone at 0.80, a speaker at 1.20 and an LCD at 1.50, totalling 6 euros before batteries, board and casing, with an estimated final cost of 8 to 9 euros. He explained that the chip's low-power wake-word mode allows about three months on three AA batteries, and the team decided on battery power and a wake word, leaving the exact wake word open. The user interface designer presented a draft command list (set, cancel, how long left, stop, add a minute); because each number uses a phrase slot, the team agreed to have numbers spoken as digit sequences, and settled the parked multiple-timer question by allowing up to two numbered timers. The team agreed on a beep plus display for feedback rather than spoken replies, confirmed a single physical button, assigned actions, and scheduled the conceptual design meeting for Wednesday at 11:00.
  decisions: The timer will use a wake word; the exact word is left open pending marketing input. The timer will be battery powered, using three AA batteries. Numbers will be spoken as digit sequences so the command set fits the chip's roughly twenty phrases. The timer will support at most two timers, numbered timer one and timer two, without custom names. Feedback will be a beep plus the display; spoken replies are on hold for cost reasons. There will be one physical button: press to stop the alarm, hold to cancel. The conceptual design meeting will be held on Wednesday at 11:00.
  actions: The industrial designer will cost the casing. The industrial designer will get a sample speaker from the supplier and test its loudness next to an extractor fan. The user interface designer will update the command list for two timers and digit-based numbers. The user interface designer will sketch the display layout. The project manager will send the minutes to the marketing expert, including the decisions on the button and battery power. The marketing expert is to email the survey results. The marketing expert is to try out wake word options with the survey participants.
  problems: The casing has not been costed, so the margin under the 10-euro production cost is uncertain, with the estimate at 8 to 9 euros. Speaker loudness over an extractor fan has not been tested. The exact wake word has not been chosen. User requirements and survey results were not available because the marketing expert was absent. Spoken replies would cost about 0.40 to 0.50 euros extra and were postponed rather than ruled out.
  action item SY0108b.ai1: Cost the casing. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0108b.ai2: Get a sample speaker from the supplier and test its loudness next to an extractor fan. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0108b.ai3: Update the voice command list for two timers and digit-based numbers. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0108b.ai4: Sketch the display layout. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0108b.ai5: Try out wake word options with the survey participants. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0108b.ai6: Email the survey results to the team. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0108b.ai7: Send the minutes to the marketing expert, flagging the decisions on the button and battery power. (owner A, active)
  fact (absence): The marketing expert (Priya) was absent from the meeting because she was off sick.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed three timers with custom names such as pasta timer; it was rejected because the chip has no free vocabulary.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested spoken replies; they were put on hold because recorded speech adds about 0.40 to 0.50 euros.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F1_OFF_TOPIC_TANGENT [F1]: A long off-topic tangent (at least 8 consecutive segments, e.g. weekend plans, a film, the coffee machine) unrelated to the project. The gold summary must NOT include the tangent's content.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.
- F1_INTERLEAVED_TOPICS [F1]: Two agenda topics are discussed interleaved: the conversation switches back and forth between topic X and topic Y at least twice each. The gold summary must present each topic coherently.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.


A PREVIOUS ATTEMPT AT THIS MEETING FAILED VALIDATION (attempt 2 of 3). Write the whole meeting again from scratch, and fix these problems:
- F1_INTERLEAVED_TOPICS: tagged segments must alternate (not one contiguous run)
